BREAKING: “BATO DELA ROSA, ARREST HIM!” Wanted posters vs. Bato lumitaw sa QC matapos ang ICC warrant issue

Nagulantang ang ilang residente at motorista sa kahabaan ng Kalayaan Avenue sa Quezon City matapos kumalat ang mga “WANTED” graffiti posters laban kay Senator Ronald dela Rosa ngayong May 18.

Ang mga posters, na ipinakalat ng militanteng grupong Akbayan Youth, ay may matinding mensahe: “BATO DELA ROSA, ARREST HIM!” at panawagang agad makipag-ugnayan sa NBI kapag nakita ang senador na iniuugnay ngayon sa umano’y ICC arrest warrant kaugnay ng madugong war on drugs ng administrasyong Duterte.

Ayon sa grupo, layunin ng kanilang campaign na hikayatin si dela Rosa na humarap sa mga alegasyon laban sa kanya sa harap ng International Criminal Court at panagutin umano sa mga kaso kaugnay ng anti-drug operations noong siya pa ang hepe ng pambansang pulisya.

Hindi lang simpleng protest action ang gustong mangyari ng grupo. Nananawagan sila ng tinatawag nilang “people’s manhunt” para tiyaking haharap si Bato sa international court.

Kasabay nito, lalo ring umiingay online ang mga tanong tungkol sa tunay na lokasyon ni dela Rosa matapos ang sunod-sunod na ulat, sightings, at political controversies na bumabalot sa Senado nitong mga nakaraang araw.

🇺🇸💥America's "Trojan Horse" Missile Deployment Strategy

Anduril Barracuda isn’t just another “cool new missile” story

It’s the U.S. turning the global shipping and logistics network into a shell game

According to multiple sources: Anduril is supplying 3,000 Container-Launched Barracuda-500M Cruise Missiles to the U.S. Army https://t.co/301AcAbJ2b

These missiles fire vertically or diagonally from standard 20-foot ISO shipping containers, the U.S. military can turn virtually any civilian flatbed truck, commercial cargo ship, or austere logistics site into a stealthy missile silo. This makes enemy tracking via satellite or traditional reconnaissance nearly impossible

Standard 20-foot ISO containers are indistinguishable from millions in global trade. This means the U.S. could pre-position thousands of missiles in allied ports, on civilian cargo ships, or even in neutral territories without detection

For China, this creates a new existential threat: missile launchers could be hidden anywhere within 926 km of Chinese territory, including ports in Japan, South Korea, the Philippines, and potentially even Hong Kong or other Greater Bay Area (GBA) ports

The “Hyper‑scale” defense production is US military‑civil fusion by another name

The scale is insane: 1,000 missiles a year starting mid-2027. At under $200,000 EACH, it's 1/10th the cost of a Tomahawk cruise missile

The real innovation isn’t the missile: It’s the factory.

Anduril built these to be assembled with 10 OR FEWER TOOLS using largely commercial components. By workers trained to build cars and smartphones. No specialized defense labor required

They basically turned the global consumer electronics supply chain into a weapons assembly line

Meanwhile the irony is almost too perfect:
Consumer electronics, semiconductors, rare earths—all those supply chains run through China

So the "resilient" missile built to fight China quietly depends on Chinese industrial inputs 

Washington is rearming for a Pacific war using the very supply chains it swears it's decoupling from 🤡 

The hypocrisy doesn't end there
The U.S. spends decades screaming about China’s "covert military deployments" accusing China of building dual use lighthouses and secret overseas military bases threatening global trade. Now the U.S. develops and deploys a system that lets them hide thousands of missiles in plain sight across the entire Indo-Pacific

Ports, logistics hubs and civilian infrastructure around the first island chain are now baked into US war plans
 
This isn’t about "defense." This is about trying to erase China’s A2/AD advantage by weaponizing the global trade infrastructure the U.S. claims to defend 

With the Anduril Barracuda missile family the US is normalizing cheap, containerized, AI‑coordinated long‑range strike as a baseline capability—which means that eventually any port, logistics park, or shipping corridor in the first and second island chains must now be treated as a potential missile farm
